_comment: How the Tribal Lands labels name a Nation, beside the Federal Register name the Impact Briefing always carries in full. nation: the Federal Register name as public/data/tribal-roster.json labelAreas holds it. ownNames (decision DR-247): the Nation's name in its own language, one row per Nation, added by hand, only from the Nation's own public pages and only where the page presents the form as the Nation's own name for itself; ownName exactly as the page writes it (capitals, apostrophes and marks kept; Unicode NFC); page, the address read; read, the date read; premise, what the page says the form is. Never from an aggregator, never translated, transliterated or corrected; a Nation whose pages give more than one form, or only a people's or language's name shared with other Nations, has no row; a new letter may need the label face re-cut (scripts/cut-nation-names-font.py; tests/font-coverage.test.mjs says so). shortNames (owner, 2026-11-13): the shorter name a Nation is generally known by, drawn on the map in place of a long formal name; shortName exactly as its source writes it; page and read, the source; basis, why this form was chosen. A Nation with no row keeps its full Federal Register name on the map.

ownNames.premise: The page is titled "The Coeur d’Alene Tribe (Schitsu’umsh)" and says: "The original name of the Coeur d’Alene Tribe was Schitsu’umsh ... This has been our name since time immemorial." The same page spells a memorial's name "Shitsu’umsh Warriors", and the site footer writes the name with a straight apostrophe; the form carried is the one the page states as the name.

ownNames.nation: Kalispel Indian Community of the Kalispel Reservation
ownNames.premise: The Tribe's home page says the name Qlispé "reflects the traditional language of the Tribe" and quotes its Executive Director of Language and Culture: "We are Qlispé. We are Camas People."

ownNames.nation: Lummi Tribe of the Lummi Reservation
ownNames.premise: The Nation's home page says: "We are the Lhaq'temish, the Lummi People." A menu entry for the Lhaqtemish Foundation, an organization's name, drops the apostrophe.
